scenario: [LFAC.2.5] tolerance-aware mutable-slot dedup — verified on the FACT STREAM. Under declared-key identity tolerance is event-observable, not count-observable: a same-key fact is a singleton (LFAC.1.7.2), so a re-assert never changes fact_count (it is a no-op or an in-place replace). Reading{zone key, celsius mutable tolerance 0.5}: assert zone=a celsius=10.0 (fact_assert); re-assert celsius=10.3 within 0.5 tolerance -> NO meaningful change -> no-op: the WM change is suppressed and the fact_id is preserved, but the assert ARRIVED and is recorded, so a second fact_assert appears (RFCS.6.7); re-assert celsius=10.8 outside tolerance -> meaningful change -> assert+retract pair, the arriving assert recorded before the retract it causes (fresh fact_id, LFAC.1.2.2, LFAC.2.5.3, RFCS.6.7). Exactly [tick, fact_assert, fact_assert, fact_assert, fact_retract] (strict) — the leading tick is the engine's first clock sample, taken by the first assert and recorded before it ([LTIM.2.8.5]); the clock does not move, so no later assert records another — a broken within-tolerance no-op would emit an extra RETRACT+assert PAIR rather than the lone assert, and fail. LFAC.2.5.1 enumerates what a suppressed reassertion does not do (dwell does not reset, no series sample, no logical flicker, a counter increments) and the recorder is not in that list. RFCS.6.7 governs uniformly: tolerance absorption is a working-memory discipline and does not reach the recorder. The atom carries the STORED value (10.0), not the arriving 10.3: 'records an assert arriving' is the EVENT, not the payload. Conformance mirror of pyds test_tolerance_runtime.
